newsitem.title: USA: GM unit sees growth in outside parts sales.
newsitem.headline: GM unit sees growth in outside parts sales.

text.p: General Motors Corp's Delphi Automotive Systems unit expects about 35 percent of its 1996 revenues to come from outside GM's North American Operations (NAO), up from just over 30 percent in 1995, Delphi President J.T. Battenberg said Tuesday.

Battenberg, speaking to reporters at an automotive supplier conference here, said Delphi's sales to non-GM NAO customers would equal about $10 billion for 1996. The non-NAO total, however, includes sales GM's overseas auto operations.
In 1995, Delphi reported total revenues of $26.4 billion, just over 30 percent of which came from non-NAO customers.

Battenberg said Delphi is currently in 167 businesses around the world. About 58 percent of its employees are located outside of the United States, a number that Battenberg said could grow in the future as Delphi expands overseas.
Battenberg said he anticipates that more suppliers will turn to alliances and joint ventures as a cost-effective way to expand in overseas markets.
He added that he and Ford Motor Co Vice Chairman Edward Hagenlocker have discussed the possibility of future components ventures between the two automakers and will continue to do so.
One of Hagenlocker's new duties as vice chairman is to reorganize Ford's components operations and improve their efficiency.
"We have a lot in common," Battenberg said of GM and Ford.
